title: Zalm (Salmon)
description: Prepared with salmon, water, and salt.

ingredients.name: 10 g salt per litre of water

steps: Scrape the scales off the salmon, wash the pieces and cook them in boiling water with not too much salt (to keep the color nice) 2 minutes per 100 grams.
Remove the pieces with the fish slice or a couple of skimming spoons from the pan, place them on the fish platter and set it for a moment in front of an open window, to make the color a brighter red.
With warm salmon serve: parsley sauce, warm mayonnaise or melted butter, with cold salmon: cold mayonnaise and salad.
Note: Shad can be treated as salmon, but can also be cooked in the manner of haddock.

title: Zandkoekjes (Sand Cookies)
description: A biscuit made with flour or cornstarch, butter or margarine, and powdered sugar or brown sugar.

ingredients.name: 300 g flour or 50 g cornstarch and 250 g flour
150 g powdered sugar or brown sugar

steps: Sift the flour or flour mixture and the powdered or brown sugar
Knead both with the butter or margarine together
Roll out the dough on a floured board with a floured rolling pin to 1/2 cm thickness
Cut out cookies with cookie cutters, cookie stamps, glasses or cups
Place them on a greased baking sheet with some distance between them
Bake them in the upper part of a moderately warm oven until lightly brown and done (approximately 15 to 20 minutes)
Remove them immediately from the baking sheet and let them cool
If the dough becomes too soft from kneading to roll out, let it stiffen on a cool place for some time covered
Alternative method: form the dough into a thick roll after kneading with the diameter of a silver guilder, let it stiffen and cut slices from it

title: Zandtaartjes en Hernhutters (Small Sand Cakes)
description: A cake made with butter or margarine, flour or cornstarch, and brown sugar.

ingredients.name: 300 g flour or 50 g cornstarch and 250 g flour

steps: Sift the flour or flour mixture into a bowl
Add the butter or margarine and brown sugar
Knead all ingredients together until no sugar granules are felt
Coat small molds (for Hernhutters use very small fluted molds) with melted butter or margarine
Fill them 3/4 full with the dough
Place on a baking sheet and bake in a moderately warm oven in the middle position until very lightly brown and done (approximately 20 minutes)
Test for doneness by inserting a larding needle, meat fork or knitting needle, which should come out dry
If the cakes brown too much during baking, cover with a piece of gray paper brushed with butter
Let the cakes cool and turn the molds over
Dust the cakes with powdered sugar after cooling

ingredients.name: 55 g white gelatin or 50 g powdered gelatin

steps: Prepare the water mixed with the sugar, the soaked gelatin, the lemon juice and the egg white in the same manner as described for aspic.

Let this cool (preferably on ice), then arrange some candied fruits, alternating in shape and color, on it, glue them with a little lukewarm gelée, let the mass cool again, pour gelée over until everything is covered and let it set.
Continue this way until the entire mold is filled.

title: Zoetzuur van Kwetsen (Sweet and Sour Plums)
description: Prepared with plums, vinegar, and sugar.
steps: Wash the plums, dry them, prick them all over with a silver fork, place them in a Cologne pot and pour over the vinegar, which has been cooked with the spices (optionally also mace) and the sugar
Let the plums stand for a week and stir them gently from time to time
Cook the plums in small batches together in the liquid until they are completely smooth without wrinkles
Carefully remove each plum that has become smooth from the liquid, place them in the Cologne pot, and when all plums are ready, pour the liquid with the spices over them
Close the pot with damp parchment paper and label it with name and date
Let them stand for at least 3 weeks before use

title: Zoute Bolletjes (Savory Rolls)
description: A bread preparation made with yeast, butter or margarine, and egg yolk.
steps: Put the flour in a warmed bowl, make a small well in the middle, add the milk and yeast, stir in about half of the flour and let this starter rise for 15-20 minutes in a warm place.
Add the melted butter or margarine, the beaten egg and the salt and knead this dough until it releases from your hands.
Throw it on a flour-dusted board and work it back and forth for 5 minutes, let it rest in a cool place for half an hour.
Flatten it, divide it into 60-65 pieces and shape them into balls.
Lay them on a greased baking sheet, flatten them slightly with a damp cloth and brush them with egg yolk beaten with a little water.
Let the rolls rise for another 15-20 minutes in a warm place, bake them in a hot oven until light brown and done (15-20 minutes). Remove them from the sheet and let them cool.

title: Zwampudding (Sponge Pudding)
description: A pudding made with butter or margarine, vanilla pod, and milk.
steps: Stir butter or margarine, flour and sugar together until all lumps are gone.
Add the milk gradually and cook the mixture on moderate heat, stirring with a whisk, until it is done and bound.
Let it cool slightly, add the egg yolks and the scraped vanilla and last as lightly as possible the stiffly beaten egg white.

Fill a warm pudding mold coated with butter or margarine and sprinkled with fine breadcrumbs 1/3 full with the mixture, close it in the usual manner and cook the pudding 2 to 2 1/2 hours in a bain-marie, but make sure the water is continuously topped up to just below the rim of the mold.
Be especially careful with a light pudding like this so that the water does not boil over when topping up.
Let it dry slightly without the lid.
Turn the pudding, which sinks quickly, onto a warmed dish and place a warmed bowl over it for transport.

title: Zwampudding (Sponge Pudding)
description: A pudding made with butter or margarine, milk, and flour.
steps: Stir butter or margarine, flour and sugar together until all lumps disappear.
Gradually add the milk and cook the mixture on a moderately warm fire, stirring with a whisk, until it is done and bound.
Let it cool somewhat, add the egg yolks and the scraped vanilla and lastly mix as lightly as possible with the stiffly beaten egg white.

Fill a warm pudding mold coated with butter or margarine and sprinkled with fine breadcrumbs one-third full with the mixture, close it in the usual manner and cook the pudding 2 to 2 1/2 hours in a bain-marie, but make sure the water is continuously topped up to just below the rim of the mold.
Be especially careful with a light pudding like this to prevent the water from boiling over when topping up.
Let it dry slightly without the lid.
Turn the pudding, which sinks quickly, onto a warmed dish and place a warmed bowl over it for transport.

title: A Two-Pound or One-Seer Plum Cake
description: A cake made with butter or water, raisins, and currants.

ingredients.name: 4 lb. or 2 seers butter, perfectly free of water
2 lb. or 1 seer good clean sugar
2 lb. or 1 seer raisins, cleaned, stoned, and dried
2 lb. or 1 seer currants, cleaned, stoned, picked, and dried
2 lb. or 1 seer Jordan almonds, blanched and sliced very fine
preserved ginger, orange-peel, lemon-peel, and pumpkin in small pieces and well dried, mixed
1 tablespoonful cinnamon, finely pounded and sifted
1 tablespoonful dried orange-peel, finely pounded and sifted
2 tablespoonfuls English caraway-seeds, cleaned and picked
1 tablespoonful mace, finely pounded and sifted
1 claret-glass brandy of the best quality

steps: Have two large glazed earthen preserving-pans; put the sugar into one and bruise it well down, breaking all the lumps
Add to it three pounds and three-quarters of butter
Throw in one by one all the yolks of the forty eggs, and throw the whites into the other preserving-pan
Mix the sugar, butter, and the yolks the whole while briskly and without ceasing
While one man is mixing these ingredients another ought to beat up the whites of the eggs unceasingly for nearly an hour
After the butter has been well mixed with the sugar and eggs, dredge in all the finely-pounded spices and the caraway-seeds
After a while dredge in the flour and soojee in small quantities at a time, well mixed
Add the currants, raisins, and preserves, with the almonds
Pour in the brandy very gradually and in small quantities at a time
Last of all add the well-beaten whites of the forty eggs, stirring very briskly to effect a perfect mixture
Fill quickly into the moulds, lined with paper and well buttered
Bake without a moment's delay in a brisk baker's oven

title: Another Recipe
description: Prepared with beef marrow, rose-water, and white of egg.

ingredients.name: beef marrow, three-quarters of a pound

steps: Clean beef marrow well from bone and fibre
Wash it in water fresh from the spring, which must be changed night and morning for ten days
Steep it in rose-water for twenty-four hours
Drain it
Take half an ounce each of storax, gum benjamin, and odoriferous cyprus-powder, two drachms of cinnamon, and a drachm of cloves
Let these ingredients be all powdered and well mixed with the marrow
Put them in a pewter pot which holds about a pint and a half
Make a paste of white of egg and flour, and lay it on a piece of linen
Place a second linen to cover the pot very tight and keep in the steam
Place the pot in a copper vessel of water, and keep it steady, so that the water may not reach or touch the covering
As the water evaporates, add more, boiling hot
Keep it boiling four hours without ceasing
Strain the pomade into small jars or boules
Cork when quite cold

title: Aspic Jelly
description: Prepared with bacon or ham, meat, and fowl.

ingredients.name: bacon bone or slice or two of ham or bacon

steps: Put into a stew-pan an ox-foot cleaned and cut up with a bacon bone or a slice or two of ham or bacon
Add any scraps of raw meat such as cutlet trimmings or a young fowl cut up as for fricassee with a few mixed vegetables as for soup
Add a cup of cold water and cover the pan
Set it on the fire, shaking it occasionally
When the pieces of meat begin to take colour, add a little more water
In about half an hour, pour in enough water to cover the contents of the pan completely
Put in a tea-spoonful of caramel and let the vessel simmer for three hours very gently
When ready, strain the liquor off into a bowl and let it get cool
Skim it carefully and add a tea-spoonful of sugar and table-spoonful of tarragon vinegar

ingredients.name: half a pint of made gravy

steps: First, be careful in cleaning them; cut the stalks down, leaving only a little of them within the hollow of the mushroom

Simmer the sauce until it is thick and rich
Add a spoonful of cream, and then strain it
Butter a silver dish liberally, place the mushrooms upon it head downwards

Place a mould on ice and pour into it a layer of the vanilla jelly half an inch thick
When set, pour in about an inch of the cream, then a layer of jelly when the cream has set, and so on until the mould is filled
Serve after it has rested on ice for an hour

a little less than one ounce of salt (30 grammes)

steps: Take about 4 lbs. (2 kilos) of thick beefsteak cut square.

Take nearly 1/4 lb. (3 hectos) of raw fat bacon, cut off the rind, which should be put aside to blanche, and then cut the bacon in strips for larding, about one-third of an inch thick, and sprinkle them with pepper.
Lard the meat, and tie it up as for the pot-au-feu.

Place the piece of meat in a stew-pan with rather less than a pint of white wine, a wine-glass of brandy, a pint of stock, a pint of water, two calves' feet already boned and blanched, and the rind of the bacon also blanched.
Put it on the fire adding a little less than one ounce of salt (30 grammes).
Make it boil, and skim it as for pot-au-feu; next, having skimmed it, add fully one pound (500 grammes) of carrots, one onion, three cloves, one faggot of herbs, and two pinches of pepper.
Place the stew-pan on the corner of the stove, cover it, and allow it to simmer very gently for four hours and a half.
Try the meat with a skewer to ascertain when it is sufficiently cooked, then put it on a dish with the carrots and the calves' feet, and keep them covered up hot until serving.
Strain the gravy through a fine tammy; remove carefully every atom of grease, and reduce it over the fire about a quarter.
Untie the beef, place it on the dish for serving, add the calves' feet each having been cut into eight pieces, the carrots cut into pieces the size of corks, and ten glazed onions.
Arrange the calves' feet, the carrots, and onions round the beef, pour the sauce over the meat keeping the surplus for the next day.

title: Bhoonee Kitcheeree
description: Prepared with onions, ghee, and rice.

ingredients.name: two chittacks or four ounces of ghee
a few slices of green ginger

steps: Cut the twelve large curry onions lengthways into fine slices
Warm the pot carefully
Warm up two chittacks or four ounces of ghee
While bubbling, throw in the sliced onions, removing them immediately they become of a bright brown colour
Set the fried onions aside
Throw in the dal and rice (having previously allowed all the water in which they were washed to drain through a colander)
Fry until the dal and rice have absorbed all the ghee
Add a few slices of green ginger, some peppercorns, salt to taste (say one dessertspoonful), a few cloves, three or four cardamoms, half a dozen bay-leaves, and as many small sticks of cinnamon
Mix well together
Add as much water only as will entirely cover over the whole of the rice and dal
Put a good-fitting cover on, and set over a slow fire, reducing the same from time to time as the water is being absorbed
Occasionally shake the pot, or stir its contents with a wooden spoon to prevent the kitcheeree from burning
Serve up quite hot, strewing over it the fried onions

description: Prepared with fat, beef suet, and bacon or chicken bones.

steps: Cut up as small as possible a quarter of a pound of fat bacon, and a quarter of pound of beef suet, and put the pieces with a bacon bone, or some broken-up chicken bones, into a stew-pan

Cook the contents of it at first gently, gradually adding heat, and finally encouraging evaporation by actual boiling, and stirring the contents of your pan to prevent them catching

title: Blanquette of Fowl
description: Prepared with fowl, stock, and sherry.

ingredients.name: a table-spoonful of cream or the yolks of two raw eggs

steps: Slightly roast a well fed fowl, covering the breast with buttered paper to prevent its burning

Carve it neatly, cutting the white meat off in nice little round fillets, and saving the wings, merry-thought, &c.
Take the bones, skin, giblets, trimmings, and coarser meat of the drumsticks, and beat them well with your pestle

Throw them into a sauce-pan, with as much clear stock as will cover them, a glass of sherry, and the usual proportion of vegetables, especially celery, a bag of savoury herbs, lime peel, and a pinch of sugar
Make an excellent fowl consomme, adding six pounded sweet and one bitter almond
When quite ready, strain it off, and thicken it as for veloute

Add a table-spoonful of cream, or the yolks of two raw eggs beaten in a cup with a little of the sauce, and stir well in as a finishing touch

title: Boiled Chops

ingredients.name: neck of mutton, trimmed into chops

steps: Choose a good neck of mutton, and trim the little chops as neatly as possible.

When done, skim, and strain it, you ought to have a breakfast-cupful of it.
Scald the tin and cool it in cold water.
Cover the bottom of the tin with slices of onion, and arrange the chops thereon.

Cover the chops with two Bombay onions sliced fine, a carrot sliced, a young turnip sliced, a stick of celery cut into half inch lengths, two tomatoes sliced and drained, and a bunch of curled parsley.
Pepper the chops pretty freely with black pepper before covering them.
Add to the broth a liqueur glass of brandy, a table-spoonful of mushroom ketchup, a salt-spoonful of salt, and the same of sugar.
Pour in the broth, and seal the lid of the tin, all round the rim, with stiff paste, fixing it securely.
Put the tin into boiling water, and keep it on the fire for two hours.
At the time of serving, the lid should be cut off, and the tin, wrapped in a napkin, should be placed upon an ordinary dish, and sent to table immediately.

title: Boiled Ham
description: Prepared with ham, carrots, and celery.

ingredients.name: fine crust raspings or pounded baked crumbs

steps: Soak the ham for twenty-four hours, changing the water at least three times
Scrub the ham well and trim it, scraping off all discolorations
Place it in your ham-kettle and cover it with cold water (for a festival a bottle of Madeira or Marsala should be poured in with the water)

title: Bouillon
description: A soup made with ribs, carrots, and turnip.

ingredients.name: piece of the ribs of beef, weighing about five pounds

steps: Purchase a nice piece of the ribs of beef, weighing about five pounds, with two carrots, a turnip, a handful of French beans, a large Bombay onion, half a head of celery (leaves and all), two leeks, and a bunch of parsley.
Detach the meat from the bones en masse, roll it up compactly, and tie it firmly with a string.
See that your soup kettle is thoroughly clean, put in the bones (chopped up) first, and place your bundle of meat above them.
Pour in cold water enough to cover the top of the meat with one and a half ounce of salt and nothing else.

Set the pot near the fire, and let the contents come as slowly as possible to the boil, skimming off every atom of scum as it rises, and adding from time to time a little cold water to retard ebullition.
Keep the vessel open throughout the operations.
Once boiling with a clean surface, cast in your vegetables (the carrots first, followed by the turnip) all nicely washed, trimmed, and cut up.
Give the soup a tea-spoonful of caramel (burnt sugar colouring), a dessert-spoonful of sugar, a dozen pepper corns, and a bag containing mixed sweet herbs (a tea-spoonful of each).
Watch the vessel narrowly, and as soon as boiling begins again, ease off the fire, and let the contents of the kettle simmer till the vegetables are nicely done.
Remove the vegetables and put the meat broth and bone back on a low fire to simmer slowly until the meat is nice and tender.
Strain the soup from the meat, and set it to cool.
When the broth is cold, take off any fat that may have risen to its surface, and return the liquor to the sauce-pan.
Cut up some of the vegetables into nice pieces and place them in the soup tureen.
Let the contents of your sauce-pan come almost to the boil, and pour them over the vegetables.
Add a dessert-spoonful of Madeira and a dried leaf or two of tarragon to improve it.

title: Briaal Soup, or Soup Elegant
description: A soup made with veal, white pepper, and celery.
steps: Cut up the two shoulders of veal small, bones and all
After washing thoroughly, boil over a brisk fire with white pepper and the best white salt
Skim well the scum that rises
Reduce the fire and allow it to simmer until the meat falls off the bones
Strain the soup and let it cool
Thoroughly free it of all fat
Return it into a clean digester and add more salt and white pepper if necessary, and some white stocks of celery
Boil it and clear it with the whites of two eggs well beaten up
Strain through flannel and set aside
Take the best and most transparent parts of a calf's head and the tongue, and boil perfectly tender without reducing them to shreds
Remove all the scum that rises to the surface
Lay the boiled tongue and meat out on a clean dish
Slice the tongue fine and cut out all manner of devices, such as diamonds, squares, circles, hearts, stars, etc.
Do the same with the best and cleanest parts of meat selected from the head
Take care that no particles of scum or other impurities be adhering to them
Where any does adhere, rinse it off in a little of the cleared soup
Place them carefully into the tureen in which it is purposed to serve up the soup
If fancy macaroni be procurable, boil a tablespoonful tender, free of all particles of dust or powder, and add to the cut-up meat and tongue
Over the meat and macaroni pour the boiling-hot soup
Add to it a wineglassful of the palest sherry and serve up hot

ingredients.name: a quarter of a pound of preserved butter

steps: Slice up the onion, and shake the rings in an ounce of melted butter at the bottom of the stew-pan

steps: Peel thickly a ripe pine-apple, remove the eyes, cut in thin and small pieces and keep ½ seer of the pieces in lime water for a few minutes
Wash with fresh water and boil them with ½ powa of raisins with a little water
On softening remove the pan off fire
Heat a little ghee in another pan and fry a few panch-forons, mustard and cardamom seeds in it
Add the mass, sugar 1 powa, a pinch of salt and a table-spoonful of lemon-juice
Boil for some time and take down when the juice is thick

title: Chicken and Tongue Pie
description: A pastry dish made with chicken, ox tongue, and mutton.

ingredients.name: six mutton cutlets from the neck

steps: Cut up a chicken as if for curry

Pack the pie thus: a dust of chopped parsley at the bottom, then the mutton cutlets, above them the slices of tongue, and the chicken at the top

title: Chicken Chaud-Froid
description: Prepared with chickens, bones, and onion.

ingredients.name: aspic or plain strong meat jelly

steps: Cover the breasts of two good-sized chickens with paper, and roast them without letting them take colour
When cold, remove the breast meat as neatly as you can, also the flesh of the thighs and drumsticks
Out of the pieces thus obtained, trim a number of neat fillets as nearly the same size as possible
Dredge a little flour over them and cover them up

Take all the bones left after the above operation, skin, necks, pinions, &c., and make a strong chicken broth with them, adding an onion, some celery, a carrot, a bunch of parsley, a few almonds, pepper, and salt, to flavour it well
When the broth is ready, strain it into a bowl and skim it
Proceed to make with it a rich veloute sauce, using for a pint of broth an ounce of butter and one of flour

Strain it and let it get cold, then add to its thickness by stirring into it one-third of its quantity of liquefied aspic, or plain strong meat jelly, and reducing it over the fire till it coats the spoon
Take it from the fire, and add the yolks of three eggs, and (if available) a table-spoonful of thick cream
Pour some of this over the pieces of chicken completely coating each piece with a thick white glaze
Put them away so that the glaze may cool and set
Prepare a border of creme de topinambours decorating the top of the mould with carrots and green peas
After steaming it, let the mould get cold, and then set it in ice
When quite cold, turn it out carefully upon a cold silver dish
Fill the hollow in the centre with the pieces of glazed chicken, introducing a slice of truffle here and there as you arrange them
Garnish the top of the chicken with cold boiled cock's comb and truffles
Let the dish remain in the ice-box until the time arrives for it to go to table

title: Chicken Curry
description: Prepared with ghee, onions, and chilies.

ingredients.name: one chittack or two ounces of ghee

title: Chicken Curry
description: Prepared with chicken, onion, and carrot.

ingredients.name: six good shallots or two small white onions
two ounces of Denmark, Normandy, or other good tinned butter
an ounce of butter or clarified beef suet

steps: Choose a nice young chicken and cut it up neatly as for a fricassee, place the pieces aside, and dredge over them a little flour.

Take all the trimmings, neck, pinions, leg bones, feet, head, and any scraps of meat that can be spared, and cast them into a sauce-pan with an onion sliced, a carrot sliced, half a dozen pepper corns, a bit of celery, a pinch of salt and one of sugar.
Cover them with cold water and make the best broth you can.
When ready, strain the contents of the sauce-pan into a bowl, and skim it clean to obtain a good breakfast-cupful of weak stock.
Make a breakfast-cupful of milk of cocoanut, or almond.
Take your stew-pan, and having sliced up six good shallots, or two small white onions, cast the rings into it with two ounces of tinned butter.
Add a finely-minced clove of garlic, and fry till the onions turn a nice yellow brown.
Add a heaped-up table-spoonful of the stock powder, and one of the paste, or, if you have not made the latter, two table-spoonfuls of the powder.
Cook the curry-stuff with the onions and butter for a minute or two, slowly, adding by degrees a wine-glassful of the cocoanut milk, and then also by degrees the breakfast-cupful of broth.
Simmer for a quarter of an hour until you have a rich, thick curry gravy or sauce.
Place the stew-pan en bain-marie.
Take a frying-pan and melt in it an ounce of butter, or clarified beef suet, add a shallot cut up small, and fry for a couple of minutes.
Put the pieces of chicken into the frying-pan, and lightly fry them.
As soon as slightly coloured, transfer the pieces of chicken to the stew-pan in which they should rest for at least half an hour, marinading in the curry gravy.
Place the stew-pan over a gentle fire, and if the liquid be found insufficient to cover the pieces of chicken, stock, if available, or water, should be added.
Encourage a gentle simmering process, during which add the bay-leaf, chutney, and sweet-acid.
If powder without fresh paste has been used, put in the pounded almond and cocoanut with a little spice and grated green ginger.
Taste the curry gravy, and if a little more acid or sweet be found necessary, make the proper correction.
As soon as the pieces of chicken have become tender and thoroughly stewed, stir in a coffee-cupful of cocoanut milk, and in three minutes the operation will be complete.

If a semi-dry or dry curry be required, further reduce the gravy by simmering with the lid off, stirring the pieces of meat continually with a wooden spoon to prevent their catching at the bottom of the pan.
When the proper amount of absorption has been attained, remove the pan and serve.

title: Chicken Pellow
description: Prepared with chicken, beef, and onions.

ingredients.name: two chittacks or four ounces of ghee
half a pound or a coonkee of the best bassrauttee or cheeneesuckur
half a dozen small sticks of cinnamon
a blade or two of mace
half a dozen bits of finely-sliced and fried bacon

steps: Take a good-sized chicken and clean, truss, and boil it with one pound of beef in two cupfuls of clean water, seasoning it with onions, ginger, and salt
When sufficiently cooked, but yet quite firm, remove the chicken, and set it and the gravy aside
Cut up twelve onions lengthways into fine slices
Warm your pot
Melt in it two chittacks or four ounces of ghee, and as it bubbles, throw in the sliced onions and fry to a light brown
Remove and set aside the fried onions
Put in half a pound or a coonkee of the best bassrauttee or cheeneesuckur, having drained away all the water in which it was washed, and fry
On the rice absorbing the ghee, throw in a few cloves, four or five cardamoms, half a dozen small sticks of cinnamon, some peppercorns, a blade or two of mace, and one dessertspoonful of salt
Mix up the whole, and pour over it the gravy in which the chicken and beef were boiled, or as much of it only as will entirely cover the rice
Close the pot immediately with a close-fitting cover, and set on a slow fire
As the gravy continues to decrease or to be absorbed, keep reducing the fire
Shake up the pot occasionally, or stir its contents, to prevent the pellow from burning
Brown the boiled chicken in a pan with ghee or butter
Place the chicken, either whole or cut up, on the centre of a dish, covering it with the pellow
Strew over it the fried onions, garnishing it besides with two hard-boiled eggs, cut into halves, or in some device, and with half a dozen bits of finely-sliced and fried bacon

title: Chicken, St. Lambert Fashion
description: Prepared with chickens, onion, and meat.
steps: Cut up two nice chickens as if for fricassee
Steep the pieces in cold water for half an hour, then drain them
Select the following pieces: the four wings, the four legs, two breasts, and four thighs, and put them aside covered up

Take all that remains (the backs, pinions, necks, livers, gizzards, and trimmings), and with an onion cut up, some pepper corns, a few spoonfuls of meat gravy, a bit of lime peel, a tea-spoonful of ketchup, and salt, make as good a pint of broth as you can
When ready, fish out the livers, and strain the broth
Put into the stew-pan the selected joints of the chickens, cover them with the strained broth, and stew them gently till done, with one carrot, and a handful of French beans
Pick out the chicken, strain the broth, and put the vegetables aside
Proceed with the broth to make a nice veloute (rich white sauce) flavoured with a dozen sweet almonds pounded, and a blade of mace
Thicken in the bain-marie with the yolks of three eggs
When satisfactory, strain and put in the pieces of chicken, heating them without boiling
Cut the carrot, French beans, with the livers you saved, into dice

When you dish the chicken, garnish your entree with them. A casserole of mashed potatoes, shaped like the pastry case of a vol-au-vent, and nicely ornamented, can hold the chicken, and the garnish should be sprinkled over the surface

description: Prepared with raisins, currants, and bread-crumbs.

ingredients.name: one pound and a half of cleaned and picked raisins

half a pound of finely-sliced mixed peel
three-quarters of a pound of finely-minced suet
three-quarters of a pound of sugar
half a teaspoonful of finely-powdered mixed spices (cinnamon, nutmeg, and mace)
half a pound of butter free of water

steps: Mix cleaned and picked raisins, currants, finely-grated bread-crumbs, finely-sliced mixed peel, finely-minced suet, and sugar well together
Mix with half a teaspoonful of finely-powdered mixed spices (cinnamon, nutmeg, and mace)
Moisten the mixture with half a pound of butter free of water, twelve eggs well beaten, and a wineglassful of brandy, stirring well the whole time
Butter a large piece of cloth or napkin and dredge it well with flour
Put the mixture into it and tie it down tightly
Boil it steadily for seven hours
Take it out of the boiler and hang it up immediately until the day it is intended to be eaten
Boil again for fully two hours, ensuring the water is boiling before the pudding is put into it
Turn it out of the towel and serve up with brandy sauce

title: Clear Mock-Turtle
description: Prepared with stock, onions, and celery.

ingredients.name: half an ox-head unskinned or a sheep's head
a quarter ounce of dried basil
half a wine-glass of mushroom ketchup

steps: Procure the stock meat as usual, and either half an ox-head unskinned, or a sheep's head, well, clean the head thoroughly, keeping the skin on, and scalding it to get rid of the hair or wool
Remove every atom of brain and wash the meat in several waters
Set it to soak awhile in cold water, and then place it in your soup kettle
Cover it with water and let it simmer slowly for an hour, skimming all fat and scum that may rise
Take it up (it will be about half done), remove the bones and set it, with a weight upon it, on a dish to flatten and get cold
Throw your shin, &c., into the soup kettle, adding to the cold head liquor already there, the bones just removed, sufficient cold water to cover the bone and meat completely and an ounce of salt
Proceed as for consomme skimming very carefully, and retarding the boiling point as much as you can by periodical additions of water

When boiling takes place, ease off the fire, and add two Bombay onions in quarters, a head of celery, a couple of carrots, the rind of two limes, a large bunch of parsley, a quarter ounce of dried basil, a teaspoonful of dried thyme, and of marjoram (the herbs in a muslin bag), a dozen pepper corns, two anchovies cut up, half a wine-glass of mushroom ketchup, a tablespoonful of sugar, and a teaspoonful of caramel
Simmer slowly now for about three hours, skimming the surface occasionally, and on no account permitting the vessel to boil
Strain very carefully, and set the soup in a bowl to cool and throw up all grease
Cut the cold head into one-and-a-half-inch squares, skim the cool soup well, and pour it into a large sauce-pan adding the pieces of head
Let the pieces cook slowly for half an hour, then drain them, and again strain the soup
Clarify it if necessary adding a glass of Madeira, and the juice of a lime
Heat this up finally when required, and pour the soup into the tureen over a dozen or so carefully selected pieces of the head arranged therein
Serve with limes cut into quarters, which should be handed round followed by the Madeira

title: Clear Snipe Soup
description: A soup made with consomme, currant jelly, and bread.

ingredients.name: a very little red currant jelly

steps: Prepare a bright clear consomme for your eight covers

Divide them into convenient pieces, mash them in a mortar and throw the whole, with the exception of the livers of the birds, into the consomme

Let it get cold, roll it out, and divide it into little portions
Form them between two tea-spoons, and poach till done just before serving the soup
Put them into the soup at the last minute

Flavour it with salt, pepper, and a little powdered thyme to taste
Stir it over the fire for three or four minutes
Take it off the fire and add two eggs beaten up with the juice of a lime and strained
Spread the mince out upon a large dish and let it get cold
Divide it into six or eight egg-shaped croquettes
Introduce in the centre of each a piece of truffle the size of a shilling
Bread-crumb them and fry them a very light gold colour
Prepare a circle of mashed potato and place it in the dish
Dispose the croquettes carefully round it
Between every croquette put a crispy fried curl of bacon
Place a slice of truffle upon each croquette
For the asparagus points, cut off the green ends of the stalks of a tin of asparagus
Heat them gently up in veloute made with the chicken broth, slightly flavoured with almond, and enriched with a good spoonful of cream
Give them a few drops of anchovy vinegar
Pour them into the middle of your potato circle

title: Croquettes of Duck à la Bordelaise
description: Prepared with duck, onion, and melted butter.

ingredients.name: minced bacon, lean and fat in equal shares

steps: Roast the bird lightly and set it to cool, then cut off all the meat from the bones, saving every atom of skin, bone, liver, &c.
Put the meat away for awhile, giving it a good dusting with black pepper and salt
Mince an onion, and one clove of garlic and stir the mince into a table-spoonful of melted butter at the bottom of a small sauce-pan

Let it fry a pale brown, now throw in all your fragments of duck, having mashed the bones in a mortar, a breakfast-cupful of strong gravy, the rind of a lime; a dozen pepper corns, a pinch of sugar, and salt to taste
Add water enough to cover the bones well, and let the contents of the sauce-pan simmer, skimming off the scum that rises
In half an hour you will have a well-flavoured broth
When quite satisfied with the broth, strain it off, let it cool, skim it, and thicken it plainly with flour and butter
Place the sauce-pan in the bain-marie-pan, and let it keep hot there
Take a tumblerful of sauterne, put it into a small sauce-pan with a table-spoonful of minced onion, a salt-spoonful of black pepper, and a pinch of salt
Boil till the liquid has been reduced to half its original quantity
Strain it into the previously made sauce
Give the whole a simmer for ten minutes and serve

title: Croquettes of Fowl Truffed
description: Prepared with fowl, stock, and onions.
steps: Roast a fair sized fowl, protecting the breast from burning by a buttered paper
When partly done, carve the bird carefully, picking on all the white meat you can
Remove the skin from these pieces and put them aside
Break up the carcass, and throw it, with all fragments of skin and bone, and the giblets of the fowl previously saved, into a sauce-pan, with as much stock as will cover the whole

Add two onions, a clove of garlic, a carrot, sweet herbs, pepper, and salt, and simmer the contents of your pan as long as you can, finally adding half a glass of sherry, and bringing the broth to the boil
Strain it, remove all fat that may rise, and reduce the sauce a little
Thicken it with butter and flour, take it off the fire, and stir in the yolks of two eggs beaten up with the juice of a lime

title: Croustades de Lapin à la Reine
description: Prepared with rolls, rabbit, and tongue or ham or bacon.
steps: Take eight stale dinner rolls, which have been lightly baked in cylindrical tins about two inches and a half in diameter.
Cut them so as to leave a case about an inch and a half deep.
Scoop out every atom of crumb, and trim the tops that you cut off neatly, so as to form a lid for the top of the hollowed rolls.
Fry the cases and their lids in butter till of a golden yellow, and set them on one side to dry.

Choose a small rabbit, some tongue ham or lean bacon, a few sweet-breads if you can get them, and have ready some cocks' combs, sliced mushrooms, a little grated lime peel, and a slice of truffle for the top of each croustade.
Remove the fillets from the rabbit's back and divide them into pieces, or cut them with a cutter about the size of a shilling.
Put the rest of the rabbit into a stew-pan with the usual vegetables to yield a good broth, and with it make a rich white sauce flavoured with some milk of almonds.
Butter a saute-pan, and cast into it your pieces of rabbit fillet with some slices of onion and carrot.

title: Croustades de Truffes à l'Espagnole
description: Prepared with espagnole, bread, and truffles.
steps: Line as many little open tartlet pans as you have guests with some carefully made short-bread paste, using an oval shape not much larger than the bowl of a table spoon.
Butter them well first to keep them from burning.
Preserve their hollow centres while baking them by a piece of stale bread, to be removed afterwards.
Cut up some truffles in dice, using enough to yield a good dessert-spoonful per head.
Warm the minced truffles gently in some rich Espagnole sauce flavoured with a dash of Madeira, and keep it en bain-marie.
When wanted, fill the crisp croustades with a spoonful each of the truffles and sauce.
Dish them en serviette, and send them round with the bird.

title: Cucumber Chutney
description: Prepared with cucumber, onion, and chilli.

ingredients.name: three heaped up table-spoonfuls cucumber strips

title: Cucumbers a la Poulette
description: Prepared with cucumber, sauce, and water.

ingredients.name: 1 good sized cucumber or 2 small ones
half a pint of poulette sauce

steps: Take a good sized cucumber or two small ones; cut them lengthwise into quarters, remove the seeds, and peel off the green skin
Cut them into pieces two inches long and one inch thick
Put them into a stew-pan with plenty of boiling water, half an ounce of butter, and a tea-spoonful of salt
Simmer them until three parts done
Drain the liquor off, and turn the pieces of cucumber out upon a clean dish
Cut each piece in half and cover them up
Make half a pint of poulette sauce, put the pieces of cucumber into it
Warm gently in the bain-marie, and serve

title: Curacao
description: Prepared with brown sugar, wine, and water.

ingredients.name: a pound of dark brown sugar-candy
a hundred and twenty drops of oil of bitter orange
a quart of spirits of wine sixty-two degrees overproof

steps: Boil a quart of water in a very clean pan
add to it, bit by bit, a pound of dark brown sugar-candy
when the latter is dissolved, increase the fire and let the syrup boil up
pour it into a deep dish to cool
dissolve a hundred and twenty drops of oil of bitter orange in a quart of spirits of wine sixty-two degrees overproof
mix with the syrup when quite cold
filter and bottle the liqueur

title: Cure's Omelette with Tunny and Herring Roes
description: Prepared with herrings, shallot, and lime juice.

ingredients.name: half a slice of preserved tunny
soft roes of two herrings a la sardine
a few drops of lime juice

steps: Finely mince together half a slice of preserved tunny and the soft roes of two herrings a la sardine with a little shallot and a dessert-spoonful of parsley.
Toss the mixture in butter awhile.
Stir into a basin containing six well mixed eggs.
Cook the mixture as already explained.
Turn it out, when ready, into a hot dish containing a little melted butter, a few drops of lime juice and some minced shallot and parsley.

title: Curry Paste
description: Prepared with chilies, mustard, and garlic.

ingredients.name: eight ounces of dhunnia, or coriander-seed, roasted
one ounce of jeerah, or cumin-seed, roasted
two ounces of huldee, or dry turmeric
two ounces of lal mirritch, dry chilies
two ounces of kala mirritch, black pepper, roasted
two ounces of rai, or mustard-seed
one ounce of soat, or dry ginger
one ounce of lussan, or garlic
four ounces of cheenee, or sugar
four ounces of chunna or gram dal without husk, and roasted
good sweet oil or mustard oil

steps: Carefully pound and grind down the ingredients in the proportions given with the best English white wine vinegar to the consistency of a thick jelly.
Warm some good sweet oil, and while bubbling fry in it the mixture until it is reduced to a paste.
Let it cool, and then bottle it.
Great care must be taken not to use any water in the preparation, and mustard oil is better adapted than sweet oil for frying the mixture in.

title: Curry Powder
description: A seasoning mixture made with mustard, chillies, and pepper.

ingredients.name: salt, a quarter of a bottle

steps: Weigh everything most carefully, and even after the various ingredients have been cleaned, weigh them again, and also weigh the husks that have been removed.
Parch the coriander-seed and fenugreek very carefully, i.e., roasted like coffee berries, before being pounded.
Clean and dry each of the other ingredients separately.
Pound each ingredient separately and sift well.
Mix the whole of the powders, sprinkling in salt by degrees during the process.
Thoroughly cleanse and dry bottles in the sun.
Fill bottles and cork tightly down, with tops securely waxed over.

Some recommend that when the powder has been mixed, it should be browned in melted butter over the fire, then dried in the sun, and powdered again, in order to tone down the strong flavour of the cummin-seed.
